blurb: A focused six-fact drill set for Science, Medicine and Mathematics Through Innovation.

topics.title: Scientific method
topics.hook: The scientific method uses observation, hypothesis, testing, and revision to investigate questions.
topics.explainer: The scientific method uses observation, hypothesis, testing, and revision to investigate questions. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Science, Medicine and Mathematics Through Innovation

connections.fact: Vaccine safety and effectiveness are evaluated through hypotheses, controlled trials, observation, and revision.
Scientific experiments use probability and statistics to judge whether observed results plausibly arose by chance.

topics.title: Vaccination
topics.hook: Vaccination trains the immune system to recognise a pathogen before serious disease occurs.
topics.explainer: Vaccination trains the immune system to recognise a pathogen before serious disease occurs. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Science, Medicine and Mathematics Through Innovation

connections.fact: Some vaccines deliver genetic instructions related to a pathogen, while DNA is the hereditary material in most organisms.
Vaccines prepare immunity before disease, whereas antibiotics treat bacterial infections after they occur.

topics.title: DNA
topics.hook: DNA carries genetic information in most living organisms.
topics.explainer: DNA carries genetic information in most living organisms. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Science, Medicine and Mathematics Through Innovation

connections.fact: DNA can encode antigens in some vaccine platforms, but vaccination is the process of training immune memory.
Bacteria carry DNA mutations or resistance genes that can make an antibiotic ineffective.

topics.title: Antibiotics
topics.hook: Antibiotics treat bacterial infections and do not treat viral infections.
topics.explainer: Antibiotics treat bacterial infections and do not treat viral infections. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Science, Medicine and Mathematics Through Innovation

connections.fact: Antibiotics act against bacteria in an existing infection; vaccines prime the immune system before exposure or serious illness.
Changes in bacterial DNA can confer antibiotic resistance and spread through reproduction or gene transfer.

topics.title: Algorithm
topics.hook: An algorithm is a finite, defined sequence of steps for solving a problem.
topics.explainer: An algorithm is a finite, defined sequence of steps for solving a problem. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Science, Medicine and Mathematics Through Innovation

connections.fact: An algorithm gives finite steps for solving a problem, while the scientific method gives a repeatable process for testing explanations.
Algorithms use probability in tasks such as risk scoring, randomised search, and statistical inference.

topics.title: Probability
topics.hook: Probability measures the likelihood of an event on a scale from 0 to 1.
topics.explainer: Probability measures the likelihood of an event on a scale from 0 to 1. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Science, Medicine and Mathematics Through Innovation

connections.fact: Probability helps researchers assess evidence and distinguish a real effect from random variation.
A probabilistic algorithm uses random choices or likelihood estimates while still following defined computational steps.

questions.q: Which sequence best represents the scientific method?
questions.explanation: Scientific inquiry moves from observations to testable explanations, gathers evidence, and revises conclusions when results demand it.

questions.q: What does vaccination prepare the body to do?
options: Recognise a pathogen before serious disease
Kill every bacterium directly on injection
Replace inherited DNA with pathogen DNA
questions.explanation: Vaccines expose the immune system to an antigen or its instructions so memory responses can act rapidly on later exposure.

questions.q: Which molecule carries hereditary information in most living organisms?
questions.explanation: DNA encodes genetic information in nucleotide sequences and passes that information through cell division and reproduction.

questions.q: Which illness would not be cured merely by taking an antibiotic?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics target bacterial structures or processes; influenza is viral and therefore needs prevention or antiviral management rather than antibacterial drugs.

questions.q: A finite sequence of unambiguous problem-solving steps is called what?
questions.explanation: An algorithm specifies a bounded, defined procedure whose steps transform inputs or state toward a result.

questions.q: On the conventional 0-to-1 scale, what probability represents an impossible event?
questions.explanation: Probability zero denotes impossibility in the elementary scale, while one denotes certainty and values between represent uncertainty.

questions.q: Why are controlled vaccine trials part of the scientific method?
options: They test safety and effectiveness claims against evidence
They prove a hypothesis before participants are observed
They remove the need for a comparison or control group
They guarantee that later evidence cannot revise a conclusion
questions.explanation: Controlled comparison lets researchers estimate effects and uncertainty instead of accepting a medical claim on authority alone.

options: Vaccines prime immune memory; antibiotics act against bacteria
Vaccines directly kill all bacteria; antibiotics train immune memory
Antibiotics prevent viral infection; vaccines treat every active infection
Vaccines and antibiotics are interchangeable pathogen treatments
questions.explanation: Vaccination is preventive immune training, while antibiotics are treatments directed at bacterial infections.

questions.q: How can DNA be linked to antibiotic resistance?
options: Resistance genes or mutations can be carried in bacterial DNA
Resistance occurs only when human DNA changes after treatment
Antibiotics prevent bacteria from inheriting any DNA
Bacterial resistance is independent of mutation and gene transfer
questions.explanation: Bacteria can inherit or exchange genetic changes that reduce a drug's effect, allowing resistant populations to survive.

questions.q: A navigation program chooses routes using estimated traffic likelihoods. Which two ideas are combined?
questions.explanation: The route procedure is an algorithm, and its uncertain traffic estimates are expressed with probabilistic information.
